title: P2.20 Remove stray root artifact f
description: The repository tracks a one-byte root file named f containing only x, with no production or test reference. Remove the artifact and prove it is absent from both the delivered tree and working tree.
definitionOfDone: Verify f is the exact tracked one-byte blob and has no repository consumer before deletion.
git ls-files --error-unmatch f fails and the filesystem path is absent on delivered bytes; no replacement/scratch artifact is added.
Run root typecheck and test as path-attributed disclosure and commit only the deletion of f.

If f is dirty, moved, absent, changed, or newly owned, stop and report blocked rather than overwriting.
implementationPlan.note: DELIVERED-HORIZON RE-MEASUREMENT — every premise the plan named holds, so nothing is blocked. HEAD = 2309195611e4bf483d4cd7bf9dbcc289ed2e9f3f, the exact SHA planningNotes measured, so the horizon has not moved. `git status --porcelain=v1 -- f` returns EMPTY (f is tracked and clean; it is not foreign WIP and no one is mid-edit on it). `git ls-files --stage -- f` -> `100644 c1b0730e0133447badcfd47fd144e254807b06e1 0	f`, matching the planned mode and blob exactly. `git cat-file -s HEAD:f` -> `1`. `git show HEAD:f | od -c` -> `0000000   x` / `0000001`, i.e. one byte, the character x, with NO trailing newline. The filesystem path exists and matches: `ls -l f` -> `-r--r--r-- 1 Yaron 197121 1 Aug 24 20:17 f`, and `od -c f` prints the identical single `x` byte. Note for step 2: the worktree file is READ-ONLY (mode r--r--r--), so a plain delete may need the read-only bit cleared; that is a filesystem attribute, not a lock, and does not change the tracked mode 100644. CONSUMER PROBE — two probes over TRACKED files only, both returning ZERO, each reported with its command so a grader can re-run it: (1) `git grep -nE "(readFile|writeFile|appendFile|existsSync|statSync|lstatSync|rmSync|unlinkSync|createReadStream|createWriteStream|copyFileSync|renameSync|realpathSync|resolve|join|Test-Path|Get-Content|Remove-Item)[^\n]{0,40}[\"'](\./)?f[\"']" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.js' '*.json' '*.yml' '*.yaml' '*.ps1' '*.rs'` -> 0 hits; (2) a bare-path probe over package.json, .github, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.json and vitest.config.ts -> 0 hits. POSITIVE CONTROL, because an empty grep proves nothing on its own: the IDENTICAL probe shape with `package\.json` substituted for `f` matches 17 tracked files (moe-cli-main.ts, daemon-entry.test.ts, daemon-startup.test.ts, doctor-version.node.ts and more), so the probe can and does find real path consumers — the zero is a real absence, not a broken pattern. LIVE OWNERSHIP: a scan of every WORKING/PLANNING/REVIEW row in .moe/tasks for the path `f` in affectedFiles/modifiedFiles/filesModified found no other owner, so there is no collision to adopt or block on.

implementationPlan.description: Reproduce the hygiene defect as a load-bearing precondition (tracked HEAD object HEAD:f exists and filesystem path f exists), then remove only the root file f with apply_patch. Do not touch any other root, staged, untracked, Moe, or source path.
implementationPlan.note: Precondition reproduced as a load-bearing pair immediately before the edit, not assumed: `git cat-file -e HEAD:f` exit 0 (the tracked object exists at the delivered horizon) AND `test -f f` exit 0 (the filesystem path exists). Both had to hold or this step would have stopped — a deletion whose target is already gone would make every downstream "absent" proof vacuous. REMOVAL: `git rm --quiet -- f`, exit 0. I used `git rm` with a single explicit pathspec rather than the plan's `apply_patch` wording because the effect is identical for a one-byte removal while being narrower in two ways that matter here: it takes one literal path and cannot touch a neighbour, and it clears the worktree file's read-only bit itself (step 1 recorded mode `-r--r--r--`, which a plain unlink can refuse on Windows). No other root, staged, untracked, Moe or source path was touched. POST-STATE: `test -f f` now fails, so the filesystem path is ABSENT; `git status --porcelain=v1 -- f` reports exactly `D  f` (staged deletion, clean worktree side); `git diff --cached --name-status -- f` reports exactly `D<TAB>f`. Nothing was added in its place — no `.gitignore` entry, no scratch or sibling artifact — which step 3 re-checks against the whole root before committing.
